Parallel parent spawned docs and CLI probes, consumed returned findings, wrote the Go implementation, rebuilt after source disruption, verified representative cases, and finalized.

Nested documentation probe summarized bundled README and docs, including CLI options, rc files, prompt variables, completion, history, and logging.
Go-engine probe evaluated the feasibility of using mvdan shell libraries, found dependencies unavailable offline, and returned an API-risk assessment.
Engine-probe child checked installed Go and Rust tooling, confirmed network dependency fetches failed, and recommended custom parser or vendored library approaches.

timeline_reviews.summary: Serial main trajectory transport stream was reviewed as manifest source 1; it carries no projected semantic events.
Serial actor independently read docs, probed CLI and shell behavior, implemented Python plus Bash runtime files, fixed prompt and parser bugs, verified, and finalized without delegation.

parallel.requirements: Recognized a clean-room replacement for nsh 0.4.2, including CLI flags, rc loading, prompt language, aliases, environment and cwd state, command execution, parsing, pipes, redirection, substitutions, and no source lookup or wrapper use.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent retained implementation ownership while spawning documentation, CLI, and engine-probing children. Children explored behavior and feasibility, and some wrote directly into the shared workspace rather than only returning isolated findings.
parallel.implementation: Produced a Go codebase with main.go, parser.go, shell.go, util.go, go.mod, compile.sh, and executable. The design hand-implemented parsing and shell execution semantics after dependency-library probes failed.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact packaged the Go implementation and executable, but integration was disrupted when the docs-probe child deleted and recreated the entry-point main.go while the parent was still building from it.
parallel.verification: Ran local compile and behavior comparisons against the original for help, version, rc behavior, non-TTY startup, parse errors, arithmetic, variable splitting, unset, command failures, and other representative cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator failed at 1535 of 2289 quality tests. The final answer identified panic-backtrace detail as a residual risk, and the lower score suggests broader shell-semantic gaps in the custom evaluator.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room replacement constraints and targeted CLI flags, rc loading order, prompt mini-language, command execution, command-not-found behavior, no-TTY warning, history and log effects.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, integration, and final verification end to end, with no subagents or delegated write paths in the serial control.
serial.implementation: Built a Python CLI/startup frontend in src/nsh_main.py with a Bash runtime layer in lib/nsh_init.bash and a compile script that installs the frontend as executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Installed the reimplementation as ./executable after moving the original aside for comparison, kept final tree focused on src, lib, compile.sh, and executable, and avoided concurrent source ownership.
serial.verification: Ran side-by-side checks on help, version, -c, script execution, rc sourcing, alias expansion, prompt rendering, and representative error cases before closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator failed at 2025 of 2289 quality tests. The final answer called out remaining byte-for-byte differences in syntax diagnostics and missing-file panic text.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room reverse-engineering constraints and the broad nsh behavior surface from docs and probes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same constraints and mapped the same visible CLI, rc, prompt, history, and command-execution obligations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The recognized requirements were largely aligned; the material difference was the implementation strategy and execution quality, not task misunderstanding.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work across docs, CLI, and engine-probe children while the parent kept main implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor for probing, implementation, integration, and verification, with no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained broader concurrent exploration but introduced shared-workspace ownership risks; serial avoided those risks by centralizing ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent and children shared a live workspace and exchanged probe findings, but no missing brief or explicit interface-contract omission explains the retained issue.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not have cross-agent briefs or handoffs; the same actor carried probe findings directly into implementation choices.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context transfer was mostly adequate, while serial had no cross-agent context boundary; the concrete problem was write ownership over the entry-point file.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented a custom Go shell, parser, and utilities, carrying parser and shell semantics in the new codebase.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a Python frontend and Bash init/runtime layer, relying on Bash for much of the shell command semantics.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial delegated complex shell semantics to an existing shell backend and scored higher; parallel hand-rolled more behavior and left more evaluator-visible gaps.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel retrieved and used multiple child findings, including docs, CLI, and engine feasibility results; no completed implementation result was left unjoined.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join and carried its own local fixes through to final installation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no retained result-lifecycle failure; the serial path was simpler because no child result lifecycle existed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had a concrete shared-workspace collision: the child removed the main.go entry point and the parent's build then failed because main.go was missing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote source, runtime, and compile files as a single actor and installed the executable without concurrent shared-source edits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the retained concurrency-specific difference: parallel suffered a deliverable-source overwrite while serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local comparisons and compile checks, but the official evaluator still failed with 1535 passes and 732 failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local source and installed-executable checks, and the official evaluator still failed but with 2025 passes and 256 failures.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verification suites were incomplete relative to hidden evaluation; serial's bash-backed approach produced higher coverage despite also missing byte-for-byte diagnostic cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent more time and many more tool/model calls across six subagents, and still closed with a failed Go implementation after recovering from workspace disruption.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in less agent time with one rollout, no subagents, and a higher but still failing official score.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's broader fan-out did not translate into a pass and added coordination overhead; serial used fewer resources and achieved materially better test coverage.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official completed evaluations show both attempts failed: parallel passed 1535 of 2289 while serial passed 2025 of 2289. There is no discordant pass/fail outcome to explain. The concrete task-solving difference is that serial used a Python CLI layer and Bash runtime to inherit broad shell semantics, while parallel hand-built a Go parser/interpreter and also experienced a child-caused entry-point overwrite during integration.
parallel_contributors: Custom Go parser/interpreter carried more shell semantics directly in project code.
Concurrent child deletion and recreation of main.go disrupted build/integration flow.
serial_contributors: Single actor maintained one implementation path and avoided shared-workspace write races.
Bash-backed runtime covered more general shell behavior and yielded higher evaluator coverage.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs left evaluator-visible shell behavior gaps, especially diagnostics and exact edge cases.
Serial's shell backend likely reduced ordinary semantic misses compared with the parallel Go implementation.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official pass/fail difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process event and the score gap is a supported comparative observation, not a proven unique root cause

candidates.reason: One probe was interrupted, but no needed unfinished child result is tied to a distinct realized adverse consequence.
No complete promotable candidate was left unfinalized; the parent produced and packaged a final executable before closure.
No child result or implementation change is shown to have been merged only after the relevant integrated verification without a closing check.
Children mainly supplied probes and feasibility findings; no completed delegated implementation was abandoned unjoined.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that remained trapped below the parent before closure.
The parent responded to failed or missing build paths and took over recovery work rather than abandoning a failed child scope.
The parent used relevant completed probe findings; no available completed result was ignored and contradicted by the final path.
The parent did not simply wait until timeout without inspection; it actively probed, edited, built, and recovered during the run.
There were shared workspace edits, but a same entry-point file deletion is directly proven and more specific by precedence.
Two agents contended over main.go, but the replacement affected the directly executed entry-point source, so Deliverable Overwrite is more specific.
The overwritten file was not merely a non-entry library or configuration source; it was the entry-point source used to build the submitted executable.
A child deleted and recreated /workspace/main.go while the parent owned and built from that entry-point source, causing visible build failure and recovery detours.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parent's compile failed because the main.go entry point was missing, then it diverted into a cmd/nsh package path and had to repair build layout.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-file contention occurred, but taxonomy precedence selects Deliverable Overwrite because main.go was the executable entry-point source.

candidates.reason: The evidence shows a targeted main.go deletion/recreation, not a broad final-tree cleanup or promotion replacing multiple outputs.
The workspace was shared, but the more specific deliverable overwrite is directly proven, so the broader label is not retained.
No generated artifact, fixture, cache, temporary path, or auxiliary tool was consumed as stable reference input by another actor.

retained_patterns.reason: A docs-probe child removed and replaced /workspace/main.go while the parent treated main.go as the entry-point source for the submitted Go executable. The parent then observed missing-main build failures and changed build layout to recover. Serial had no subagents and implemented one owned src/lib path.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parent lost the expected entry-point source during build, saw stat/no-main errors, and spent recovery work moving through an alternate cmd/nsh package layout.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is a near match, but the affected file was the directly executed entry-point source for the delivered executable, which the taxonomy classifies as Deliverable Overwrite.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Same-File Collision, Source Overwrite, Cross-File Scope Collision, and Unisolated Workspace Writes are suppressed as less-specific descriptions of the same main.go overwrite chain.
Load-imbalance and timing symptoms from the same disruption are not retained because the direct write boundary is the corrective point.
